_comment: Reusable evidence library that the long-form-article-architect skill draws from when writing articles. Populate this with REAL citations the brand can authentically claim. Generic citations weaken E-E-A-T audits — specificity is the whole point.
_structure: Each entry has a category (experience/expertise/authority/trust), a topic_tags array (so the architect can find relevant evidence per article), the actual evidence content, source attribution, and a usage_note explaining how to integrate it.

evidence_pool.evidence: In Q2 2025 we worked with a 200-seat B2B SaaS company that reduced 90-day churn from 14% to 6.2% by replacing their automated onboarding flow with a 1:1 success manager touchpoint at days 7, 21, and 60.
evidence_pool.source: Internal case study, customer named in published version
evidence_pool.usage_note: Use as a primary specific in articles about onboarding or churn. Include the specific numbers — vague claims ('we've seen massive improvements') trigger E-E-A-T audit failures.

evidence_pool.evidence: Our analysis of 847 B2B blogs over 12 months found that publication consistency (same day each week) correlated more strongly with organic traffic growth (r=0.61) than publication volume alone (r=0.34).
evidence_pool.source: Original research published [date], methodology in appendix
evidence_pool.usage_note: Use when arguing for editorial discipline. Always link to the underlying methodology — research without methodology fails Trust audit.

evidence_pool.evidence: Customer's VP Sales (former Salesforce enterprise AE, 12 years) on why MEDDPICC outperforms BANT for $100k+ ACV: 'BANT optimizes for finding deals you can close. MEDDPICC optimizes for finding deals worth closing.'
evidence_pool.source: Quote used with permission, contributor bio in author box
evidence_pool.usage_note: Direct quotes from named experts with verifiable credentials clear the Authority bar instantly. Don't paraphrase to avoid attribution — the attribution IS the value.

evidence_pool.evidence: Median annual contract value across surveyed B2B SaaS in our cohort (n=312, ARR $1M-$50M): $8,400. 75th percentile: $24,000. The frequently cited '$50k average ACV' figure overstates the market by roughly 6x.
evidence_pool.usage_note: Use when correcting a category misconception. Trust signals come from being willing to disagree with conventional wisdom AND showing your math.

evidence_pool.evidence: Across 14 ecommerce accounts we audited in 2025, the median creative had a useful life of 23 days at >$5k/week spend before fatigue set in. Top-quartile creatives lasted 41 days; bottom-quartile fatigued in 12.
evidence_pool.source: Internal audit dataset, methodology available on request
evidence_pool.usage_note: Specific median + quartile + sample size beats round-number assertions every time. The audit will reward this structure.

_how_to_add_evidence: The architect skill scans this file by topic_tags. Add entries whenever you produce new case studies, run new research, or capture a quotable expert insight. Aim for 30-50 entries within 6 months of running the workflow — the per-article quality bar rises measurably as the library grows.
_anti_patterns: DO NOT add evidence you cannot defend if challenged. The architect will use these citations and the audit will check them.
DO NOT add generic platitudes ('Studies show that customer experience matters'). The audit detects and rejects these.
DO NOT add evidence without attribution. Trust failures come from unattributed claims.
DO NOT recycle the same case study across 20 articles. Use case_001 for onboarding articles only; build separate case studies for separate topics.
